channel.title: Music Lessons
channel.description: Short narrated lessons on music styles, each followed by example tracks.
channel.itunes:author: Music Lessons

item.title: Japanese Jazz Fusion 1: The sound, and where it came from
item.description: How Japan built its own fusion scene, the four traits that define it, and the pioneers who opened the door.

item.title: Japanese Jazz Fusion 2: Sadao Watanabe, the elder statesman
item.description: The saxophonist who connected Japanese jazz to the world, from bossa nova and Africa to sunny Los Angeles fusion.

item.title: Japanese Jazz Fusion 3: Masayoshi Takanaka, the guitar that sings
item.description: Takanaka's vocal, tropical guitar, his Latin obsession, and the showman behind it.

item.title: Japanese Jazz Fusion 4: Casiopea, the precision machine
item.description: Casiopea's ensemble playing: unison lines, slap bass, busy drums and synthesizers, and why fans see them as the heart of the scene.

item.title: Japanese Jazz Fusion 5: T-Square, the anthem makers
item.description: T-Square's wind-synth lead, Masahiro Andoh's anthems, and how their music reached TV, school bands and video games.

item.title: Japanese Jazz Fusion 6: Kazumi Watanabe, the virtuoso
item.description: The guitarist who broke the rules of the style: harder, darker, more technical, and closest to American fusion.

item.title: Japanese Jazz Fusion 7: Spin-offs: when band members go solo
item.description: What happens when the players behind Casiopea and T-Square step out on their own, and what that reveals about each musician.

item.title: Japanese Jazz Fusion 8: Legacy: city pop, the internet and the heirs
item.description: How fusion fed city pop, how the internet rediscovered it decades later, and who carries the sound today.
